title: Base change under flat finitely presented morphisms with geometrically reduced fibres
statement:
Consider a Cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]
\[
\begin{array}{ccc}
X&\xleftarrow{h}&Y\\
f\downarrow&&\downarrow e\\
S&\xleftarrow{g}&T
\end{array}
\qquad Y\cong X\times_S T.
\]
Assume that $f$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and each scheme-theoretic fibre $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is geometrically reduced over $\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. For every abelian sheaf $F$ on $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], the canonical base-change morphism
\[
\beta_F:f^{-1}g_*F\longrightarrow h_*e^{-1}F
\]
is an isomorphism. Here inverse and direct images are those of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The morphism is the underived exchange [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] on the square with the horizontal and vertical sides exchanged: it is the adjoint under $h^{-1}\dashv h_*$ of $h^{-1}f^{-1}g_*F\cong e^{-1}g^{-1}g_*F\xrightarrow{e^{-1}\varepsilon_g}e^{-1}F$. There is no restriction on $g$ and no torsion hypothesis on $F$.

proof.text: Let $U_Z$ denote passage from abelian sheaves on $Z_{\Et}$ to sheaves of sets. By clauses (2)--(3) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures], for each edge $u$ the identifications $Uu^{-1}\cong u^{-1}U$ and $Uu_*=u_*U$ preserve the adjunction bijections and units. They also preserve counits: a counit is the adjoint of the identity, and the adjunction bijections agree. The abelian inverse-image composition comparison $c_{u,v}$ is the unique isomorphism carrying the unit of the composite adjunction to the unit of the composite, transported along the fibre-product identification of direct images, by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]; the set-valued one is the unique morphism with the same property on sections, by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]. Since forgetting preserves the units and the direct-image identifications, the forgotten abelian $c_{u,v}$ has the set-valued property, so it is the set-valued comparison by that uniqueness. The specified square isomorphism of the Cartesian square is $\theta=c_{g,e}^{-1}\circ c_{f,h}$ after $f\circ h=g\circ e$, by the description of $\theta_\square$ in [lem-weil-pbc-square-iso-pasting] (with its $f,g,f',g'$ equal to the present $g,f,h,e$); hence the canonical square comparison is preserved too. Therefore the underlying set morphism of $\beta_F$ is the set-valued canonical base-change morphism for $U_TF$. Indeed, under $h^{-1}\dashv h_*$ its transpose is exactly $h^{-1}f^{-1}g_*U_TF\cong e^{-1}g^{-1}g_*U_TF\xrightarrow{e^{-1}\varepsilon_g}e^{-1}U_TF$, the defining transpose of [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange]. Uniqueness of adjoint transposes gives equality of these arrows. This checks the canonical map as well as its source and target.

proof.text:
To compare the two adjunction descriptions explicitly, put $G=U_TF$, $L_u=u^{-1}$ and $R_u=u_*$ for set sheaves, and identify $R_fR_h=R_gR_e$ by the canonical fibre-product identifications. Put $A=R_gG$, $B=L_eG$ and $\alpha:L_hL_f\cong L_eL_g$ as in Step 1. Let $m:L_fA\to R_hB$ be the underlying arrow of $\beta_F$; thus $m=R_h(L_e\varepsilon_{g,G}\circ\alpha_A)\circ\eta_{h,L_fA}$. The composite-unit characterization in [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] gives
\[
R_fR_h(\alpha_A)\circ R_f(\eta_{h,L_fA})\circ\eta_{f,A}
=R_g(\eta_{e,L_gA})\circ\eta_{g,A}.
\]
Indeed both sides are the unit for $f\circ h=g\circ e$ after the indicated composition comparisons; clause (1) specifies their values on every section of $A$. Therefore the $L_f\dashv R_f$ transpose of $m$ is
\[
\begin{aligned}
R_f(m)\circ\eta_{f,A}
&=R_gR_e(L_e\varepsilon_{g,G})\circ R_g(\eta_{e,L_gA})\circ\eta_{g,A}\\
&=R_g(\eta_{e,G})\circ R_g(\varepsilon_{g,G})\circ\eta_{g,R_gG}\\
&=R_g(\eta_{e,G}).
\end{aligned}
\]
The second equality is naturality of $\eta_e$ applied to $\varepsilon_{g,G}$; the third is the $L_g\dashv R_g$ triangle identity. This is precisely the transpose defining the canonical arrow in [sbc-lem-degree-zero-flat-base-change], so uniqueness of adjoint transposes identifies its arrow with $m$. Apply [sbc-lem-degree-zero-flat-base-change] to the underlying sheaf of sets $U_TF$ and the given Cartesian square. Its hypotheses are exactly flatness and local finite presentation of $f$ and geometric reducedness of every fibre; no condition on $g$ is required. Its conclusion says that the canonical set-valued arrow $f^{-1}g_*U_TF\to h_*e^{-1}U_TF$ is an isomorphism. The preceding calculation identifies this with the underlying arrow of $\beta_F$, so its map on sections over every object of $X_{\Et}$ is bijective.

proof.text: For each etale object $V\to X$ let $a_V$ be the inverse of the bijective group homomorphism $\beta_F(V)$. It is additive: if $x,y$ have preimages $x',y'$, then $\beta_F(V)(x'+y')=x+y$, so uniqueness of preimages gives $a_V(x+y)=a_V(x)+a_V(y)$; and $\beta_F(V)(0)=0$ forces $a_V(0)=0$. For an etale-site arrow $W\to V$, let $r_P,r_Q$ be the restriction maps of the source and target sheaves. Naturality of $\beta_F$ gives $\beta_F(W)r_Pa_V=r_Q\beta_F(V)a_V=r_Q=\beta_F(W)a_Wr_Q$. Injectivity of $\beta_F(W)$ gives $r_Pa_V=a_Wr_Q$, the required naturality. Thus the $a_V$ form a morphism of abelian sheaves, since these are natural transformations of the underlying abelian presheaves [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Objectwise the two composites with $\beta_F$ are identities. Consequently $\beta_F$ is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves.
